title: Lesson 11: Probability Foundations and Bayesian Inference

slides.title: Reasoning under uncertainty starts with a probability model

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: Lesson eleven begins where certainty ends. An AI system rarely receives a complete, perfectly accurate world state. A medical agent sees symptoms, a robot receives noisy sensors, and a weather system sees measurements rather than tomorrow itself. Probability gives us a disciplined language for representing what could be true and how strongly the available evidence supports each possibility.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Lesson eleven begins where certainty ends. An AI

focuses.phrase: Lesson eleven begins where certainty ends. An AI
focuses.label: Core concept

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: The path on this slide has four jobs. Represent uncertain variables and their possible values. Compute joint, marginal, and conditional probabilities. Update beliefs with Bayes' rule. Then interpret the result without quietly converting association into causation. Think of the probability model as a bridge: evidence enters on one side, and a distribution over plausible hidden states leaves on the other.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: A probability of point seven is not a tiny oracle shouting seventy percent certainty. It is a claim made inside a model, using assumptions and evidence that can be questioned. If new evidence arrives, the belief should move. Our recurring audit will be: what is observed, what is hidden, what model connects them, and what exact calculation justifies the update?

focuses.label: Boundary and transfer

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Here is the practical transfer. A spam filter, navigation agent, and medical screener may all produce probabilities, but the variables and consequences differ. The numerical machinery does not decide what counts as evidence or which errors matter. Before trusting a posterior, inspect data collection, domain definitions, and calibration. A model whose seventy-percent predictions are correct only forty percent of the time has not discovered a bold new interpretation of arithmetic; it is miscalibrated.

slides.title: Evidence is observed; target variables are hidden; a model connects them

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: Separate three roles. Evidence variables are observed now: a sensor reading, a symptom, or a report of rain. Target variables are the hidden quantities we want to infer: an object's location, a disease state, or tomorrow's weather. The model describes how those known and unknown quantities relate. Without the model, evidence is merely a fact looking for a job.

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: For a self-driving car, a camera patch and lidar return are evidence. The hidden target might be whether a pedestrian occupies the lane. A model connects visual patterns and distances to that hidden state, producing a belief distribution rather than a single unqualified answer. The four bars illustrate that several states may retain probability at the same time.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: The arrow is inferential, not magical. If the model omits glare, unusual clothing, or a broken sensor, its posterior can be confidently wrong. Probability helps us expose uncertainty; it does not disinfect bad assumptions. Always name the evidence, target, and relationship separately, because mixing them is how a plausible story sneaks into the lab wearing a fake data badge.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Try the three-role test on voice recognition. The sound waveform is evidence, the intended word is hidden, and an acoustic-language model connects them. Several word sequences may remain plausible. Context can shift their probabilities without changing the recorded sound. This is why a system can revise an earlier transcription after hearing the end of a sentence: later evidence changes belief over the hidden sequence.

slides.title: Random variables name uncertain aspects; distributions assign probability to their values

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: A random variable is a function that names an uncertain aspect of the world and maps outcomes to values. R might ask whether it rains and take true or false. T might take hot or cold. Drive time D is continuous over nonnegative values, while robot location L ranges over coordinates. The variable is the question; one value is a possible answer.

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: A domain lists legal values. A probability distribution assigns mass or density across that domain. The weather table places point six on sun, point one on rain, point three on fog, and effectively zero on meteor. Those values must be interpreted together. Saying weather equals sun is one outcome; saying P of weather is a distribution describes the whole uncertain menu.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: Use a restaurant metaphor. The random variable is the menu category, the domain is the list of dishes, and the distribution is how likely customers are to order each dish. A continuous variable is more like soup volume: individual exact values need densities and intervals. Do not confuse the menu with today's order, unless you enjoy receiving seventeen entrees and a probability-theory bill.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: One more distinction matters for continuous variables. For discrete weather, probabilities attach to individual values. For drive time, probability usually belongs to an interval, such as between twenty and twenty-five minutes; the probability of one exact real number may be zero even though that number is possible. A density is not itself a probability. Integrating density over an interval produces probability, just as a height map needs area before it tells us volume.

slides.title: A valid joint distribution covers every complete assignment

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: A joint distribution is a complete ledger over assignments to several variables. For temperature and weather, each row specifies both values: hot and sun, hot and rain, cold and sun, or cold and rain. These are complete assignments. A row that says only hot is incomplete because weather is still unspecified.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: A joint distribution is a complete ledger over

focuses.phrase: A joint distribution is a complete ledger over
focuses.label: Core concept

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: Two constraints make the table legal. Every probability must be nonnegative; negative probability would be like owing three tenths of an outcome to the universe. Second, all complete rows must sum to one because exactly one complete assignment occurs. Here point four plus point one plus point two plus point three equals one.

kinetics.label: The complete probability ledger

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: Table size grows as the product of domain sizes. If variable X i has domain size d i, the joint contains the product of all d i rows. The shortcut d to the n works only when every variable has the same domain size. This growth is the first warning that full joint tables become enormous: probability is tidy, but its spreadsheet can become a small planet.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Table size grows as the product of domain

focuses.phrase: Table size grows as the product of domain
focuses.label: Boundary and transfer

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Now scale the table. Ten binary variables require two to the tenth, or one thousand twenty-four rows. Thirty binary variables require more than one billion. This combinatorial growth motivates factorization and graphical models: represent local relationships instead of writing every complete assignment explicitly. The joint distribution remains the semantic foundation, while compact structure becomes the engineering survival kit. We will use the chain rule later to show how that factorization begins.

slides.title: A joint model makes the probability of any event computable

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: An event is a set of complete outcomes. Hot and sun identifies one row, so its probability is point four. Hot alone identifies two rows because weather may be sun or rain, so we add point four and point one. The general rule is to sum the probability of every complete outcome that satisfies the event.

focuses.phrase: An event is a set of complete outcomes.
focuses.label: Core concept

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: For hot OR sun, include hot-sun, hot-rain, and cold-sun. Add point four, point one, and point two to get point seven. The hot-sun row satisfies both descriptions, but it is still one physical row. Counting it twice is like charging the same student twice because they are both a computer-science major and hungry.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: A useful procedure is mechanical: translate the query into a membership test, mark each satisfying row, and add each marked mass once. AND narrows to intersections; OR creates unions; leaving a variable unspecified gathers multiple rows. The joint model earns its keep because every event query becomes careful bookkeeping rather than storytelling.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Compare OR with the addition rule P of A union B equals P of A plus P of B minus P of A intersection B. The subtraction removes the duplicate overlap created when two event totals were added. Row selection and the formula are the same logic viewed from different distances. On a tiny table, marking rows is safer; on symbolic events, inclusion-exclusion is compact. Either way, overlap gets exactly one seat.

slides.title: A marginal distribution collapses a joint table by addition

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: Marginalization removes a variable from a joint table by summing over its possible values. To find P of hot, keep temperature fixed at hot and add across weather: point four plus point one equals point five. To find P of cold, add point two plus point three, also point five.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Marginalization removes a variable from a joint table

focuses.phrase: Marginalization removes a variable from a joint table
focuses.label: Core concept

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: The notation P of x equals the sum over y of P of x comma y says exactly that. We are not deleting evidence or averaging rows; we are collecting every complete world compatible with x. Imagine checking hotel occupancy by floor: to get the building total, add every room count without caring which room number supplied it.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: The notation P of x equals the sum

focuses.phrase: The notation P of x equals the sum
focuses.label: Worked meaning

kinetics.label: Sum out what you do not ask about
kinetics.text: Sum out what you do not ask about

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: The X marginal is point five and point five. The Y marginal is point six for plus y and point four for minus y. Each marginal distribution must sum to one. That is a powerful checksum. If it does not, a row vanished, a row was counted twice, or arithmetic took an unscheduled vacation.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Marginalization can also eliminate many variables: P of x equals the sum over every assignment to y and z of P of x, y, z. Computationally, the order of those sums can matter enormously when a model is factorized, even though the final probability does not change. Variable elimination exploits that fact. Today's table addition is the small, transparent ancestor of inference algorithms used in Bayesian networks.

slides.title: Conditioning restricts the population; it does not imply time or causation

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: Conditional probability asks about A inside the restricted world where B is true. The formula P of A given B equals P of A intersection B divided by P of B. The numerator is the mass satisfying both; the denominator rescales the entire B population to one.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Conditional probability asks about A inside the restricted

focuses.phrase: Conditional probability asks about A inside the restricted
focuses.label: Core concept

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: Among people who cough, what fraction are sick is P sick given cough. Among people who are sick, what fraction cough is P cough given sick. These denominators describe different reference populations, so the values can be dramatically different. Reversing the vertical bar is not a harmless typographical yoga pose.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: The word given does not automatically mean earlier, caused by, or morally responsible for. It means conditioned on. A diagnostic symptom may be evidence about a disease, but the conditional calculation alone does not establish causal direction. Always translate the notation into an among-the-cases-that sentence; the denominator then becomes visible in plain English.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Conditional probability becomes undefined when P of B is zero because there is no reference population to normalize. In continuous models, conditioning on exact values requires densities or more careful definitions. For our finite tables, the safety rule is simple: check that the denominator is positive, name it in words, and verify the resulting conditional values sum to one. Denominators deserve background checks too.

segments.text: Conditioning is like changing the guest list before calculating proportions. Once only plus-y guests enter the room, every percentage is computed inside that room. segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: Compare P of weather given hot with P of weather given cold. The distribution changes because temperature is informative about weather in this model. If the two tables were identical, weather and temperature would be independent: learning temperature would not change weather belief. Independence is therefore a statement about unchanged conditionals, not a vague claim that variables have never met at a conference.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: Think of zooming into a photograph. Selection crops to the evidence region; normalization enlarges that crop to fill the frame. Nothing outside the crop survives, but relationships inside it remain proportional. This procedure is Bayes' denominator in miniature: gather all ways the evidence can occur, then divide the favored way by the complete evidence mass.

visualDesign.focusPhrase: Think of zooming into a photograph. Selection crops

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: The select-normalize routine generalizes to any finite conditional query. First zero out incompatible assignments. Second sum what remains to obtain the normalizer. Third divide every surviving mass by that sum. This is sometimes written with proportionality: P of query given evidence is proportional to the joint mass consistent with both. The missing constant is not mysterious; it is precisely the amount required to make the surviving distribution sum to one.

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: Three fair coin tosses create eight equally likely sequences. The sample space contains HHH through TTT. Event A is the set with more heads than tails; event B is the set whose first toss is H. An event is a collection of outcomes, not a numerical measuring device.

segments.text: The distribution one-three-three-one comes from combinations. Exactly two heads can occur as HHT, HTH, or THH, three sequences; exactly one head also has three placements. Evidence changes the sample space before it changes the fraction.

segments.text: Three dealers have priors point two, point four, and point four. The probability of purchasing product a one differs by dealer. To infer dealer two after seeing the purchase, compute dealer two's joint mass and divide by the total probability of that purchase across all dealers.

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: We will expose numerator, normalizer, and posterior separately. This prevents a common error: normalizing by one convenient competitor instead of by every mutually exclusive way the evidence could occur.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: The three dealer terms illustrate a reusable denominator pattern. For each hypothesis, multiply prior by evidence likelihood. Store those unnormalized weights. Add all weights. Divide each by the sum. Computing the whole posterior distribution, not only dealer two, would yield point one two five, point five, and point three seven five. Their sum is one, providing the final audit.

slides.title: Represent uncertainty, compute an update, and defend the interpretation

segments.label: Core concept
segments.text: The closing audit has three stages. Represent: define variables and domains, then verify that a joint distribution is nonnegative and normalized. Infer: select or marginalize compatible rows, compute the evidence normalizer, and apply the correct product, conditional, or Bayes rule.

segments.label: Worked meaning
segments.text: Interpret: state the reference population and distinguish event from random variable, posterior from likelihood, association from cause, and MAP from maximum likelihood. A correct number with the wrong sentence is not a correct probabilistic answer; it is arithmetic wearing someone else's name tag.

segments.label: Boundary and transfer
segments.text: When you meet a new uncertainty problem, resist formula roulette. Draw the variables, identify observed and hidden quantities, write the target conditional, and list the mutually exclusive routes to the evidence. Then calculate and check bounds, normalization, and meaning. Probability becomes manageable when every symbol has a job and every denominator has an address.

segments.label: Detailed transfer
segments.text: For the next lesson, bring one real case in which a prior changes the selected hypothesis. State the hypotheses, evidence, likelihood intuition, and why unequal base rates matter. Avoid examples where the prior is merely prejudice disguised as mathematics; priors need empirical or defensible grounding. A good probabilistic argument makes assumptions inspectable, updates them with evidence, and states what uncertainty remains after the calculation.
